", "signature": "", "type": "thinking"}, {"text": "The investigation is complete. I've answered all three questions at the CloudFront/WAF boundary with full WAF-log evidence, and handed the actionable control gaps to the mitigation specialist (running in the background).

**One investigation gap to note:** whether the card-testing POSTs to `/checkout/payment` actually succeeded at the application (i.e., resulted in authorized charges / card validations) cannot be determined from WAF logs — `responsecodesent` is null for ALLOW pass-through requests, so WAF does not record the origin's response. Confirming the application-level outcome would require the origin's logs (the EKS "ui" service / ALB in us-west-2), but those pod logs are ~6 days old and almost certainly rotated out, so this outcome is not recoverable from available data. The WAF layer definitively shows the requests *reached* the origin (were allowed through); their success/decline rate at checkout is unknown.

## Summary

Across **2026-10-10 17:00:00–18:15:00 UTC**, all ~169,927 requests to `d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net` came from **4 source IPs**, each a distinct attack archetype:

**Malicious & STOPPED (✅ WAF working):**
- **sqlmap injection** (`198.51.100.60`) — SQLi (`UNION SELECT username,password FROM users--`) + XSS probes → **100% blocked (225/225)** by CommonRuleSet.
- Part of the **secret-file scanner** (`198.51.100.20`) — 25 signature-matching probes blocked.

**Malicious & GOT THROUGH (⚠️ control gaps):**
- **Card testing** (`198.51.100.30`) — 1,350 POST `/checkout/payment` in a 5-min burst → **100% allowed**.
- **Volumetric flood / payment abuse** (`198.51.100.10`, Artillery) — 168K requests incl. 9,262 payment POSTs → **100% allowed**.
- **Scanner** (`198.51.100.20`) — 200/225 signatureless probes → **allowed**.

**Why it got through (root cause):** the WAF's abuse controls aren't enforcing — the rate-based rule `AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300` is **Count-only (not Block)**, there is **no bot-control/CAPTCHA/per-endpoint rate limit on `/checkout/payment`**, and AntiDDoS only challenges under active DDoS. Signature-based blocking caught the overt injection/scan traffic, but high-volume automation and signatureless payment abuse passed unimpeded. The mitigation subagent is drafting fixes (rate rule Count→Block as the top priority, payment-endpoint protection, and an optional IP deny-list) — its proposal will arrive as its own artifact.", "type": "text"}], "user_reference": null}

# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### ~170k-request traffic spike on CloudFront EEXAMPLE000001
**Description:** Over 2026-10-10 17:00–18:15 UTC the distribution saw ~169,927 requests (~37 req/s), ~99% from a single IP — the volume that prompted this investigation. No origin errors or availability impact observed; WAF allowed 169,677 and blocked 250.
**Time:** 2026-10-10T17:00:00Z - 2026-10-10T18:15:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: Dominant traffic is an Artillery load test (198.51.100.10)
**Description:** IP 198.51.100.10 sent ~168,126 requests (~99% of all traffic) at a steady ~11k requests per 5-min bucket (~37 req/s) across the entire 17:00–18:15 UTC window. The requests carry the User-Agent 'Artillery (https://artillery.io)' and hit realistic e-commerce paths (GET /cart, GET /catalog, GET /home, POST /cart, POST /checkout, POST /checkout/payment, POST /checkout/delivery, GET /catalog/<uuid> product pages — 15 distinct URIs per bucket). This is synthetic load-test traffic, NOT an attack. The WAF rate-based rule (300 req/5min/IP) is in Count mode, so it logged but never throttled it.
**Cascades to:** symptom-traffic-spike

#### Gaps
- **Rate-based rule is Count-only, so floods and bursts are never throttled:** AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront is Action=Count (not Block). Both the 168k single-IP Artillery flood and the 1,350-POST card-testing burst exceeded 300/5min but were only counted. Switching to Block (or allowlisting the authorized test IP) would throttle synthetic/abusive floods at the edge.

### Cause: Card-testing burst on /checkout/payment got through (198.51.100.30)
**Description:** 198.51.100.30 (spoofed Chrome 141 UA) sent 1,350 POST /checkout/payment in a single ~5-minute burst at 18:05, with small varying 76–82-byte bodies (different card data per request). All 1,350 were ALLOWED — no injection signature, so the signature-only managed rule groups did not match, and no bot-control/CAPTCHA or per-endpoint rate limit exists on the payment path.
**Cascades to:** symptom-traffic-spike

#### Gaps
- **No bot-control / CAPTCHA / per-endpoint rate limit on /checkout/payment:** Browser-UA card testing with no injection signature passes the signature-only managed groups untouched. The default action is Allow and AntiDDoS challenges only under active DDoS (SensitivityToBlock=LOW, exempts /api/ + static); 125,855 'challengeable' requests were allowed. A targeted rate limit or Bot Control/CAPTCHA on the payment endpoint would deter card testing.
- **Rate-based rule is Count-only, so floods and bursts are never throttled:** AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront is Action=Count (not Block). Both the 168k single-IP Artillery flood and the 1,350-POST card-testing burst exceeded 300/5min but were only counted. Switching to Block (or allowlisting the authorized test IP) would throttle synthetic/abusive floods at the edge.
- **Whether the card-testing POSTs succeeded at the origin is unknown:** WAF confirms the 1,350 (and the Artillery) /checkout/payment POSTs reached the origin, but it does not record the origin's response (responsecodesent is null for ALLOW pass-through). Determining the application-level outcome (authorized charges / card validations / declines) requires the EKS 'ui' service / ALB logs in us-west-2, which are ~6 days old and almost certainly rotated out — not recoverable from available data.

### Cause: Recon/attack traffic from two IPs — all injection attempts blocked
**Description:** Two low-volume hostile sources, cleanly separated from the load test. **198.51.100.60** — user-agent **sqlmap/1.8.2** — sent XSS and SQLi probes against GET /catalog (search=<script>alert(1)</script>, img onerror, javascript:, and id=1 UNION SELECT username,password FROM users--); all 225 requests BLOCKED by CommonRuleSet (BadBots_Header / GenericLFI). **198.51.100.20** — Chrome UA — scanned secret/credential paths (/.env, /.aws/credentials, /wp-config.php.bak, /web.config under /dev /old /test /backup); 25 matched signatures and were BLOCKED, 200 non-matching variants were ALLOWED (returned non-existent). No injection payload reached the origin.
**Cascades to:** symptom-traffic-spike

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Harden WAFv2 Web ACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 to close the rate/abuse control gaps that let malicious traffic through CloudFront EEXAMPLE000001

## Reasoning
The Web ACL's default action is Allow and its only rate control (AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300, 300/300s per IP) is Action=Count — it counts but never blocks. So the 168k single-IP flood and the 1,350-POST /checkout/payment card-testing burst both blew past the threshold yet were 100% allowed; the scanner got 200/225 probes through. Three changes, priority order: (A) rate rule Count→Block; (B) scoped-down rate Block rule on /checkout/payment; (C) IP set + Block rule for the two confirmed-malicious IPs. All five managed rule groups and priorities preserved. CAVEAT: 198.51.100.10 (Artillery) is likely a sanctioned load test — it is deliberately NOT deny-listed, but gap A will throttle it by volume, so confirm with the load-test owner before applying gap A. 198.51.100.60 (sqlmap) is already fully blocked and needs no action.

## Execution Plan

### Step 1: Prepare

#### 1.1 Capture the complete current Web ACL (full Rules array, DefaultAction…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 > waf-webacl-backup-$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).json
```
**Purpose:** Capture the complete current Web ACL (full Rules array, DefaultAction, VisibilityConfig) as the exact baseline the rollback restores. CLOUDFRONT-scope calls must target us-east-1.
**Advisory:** Verify the backup corresponds to Id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 before relying on it for rollback.

### Step 2: Pre Validate

#### 2.1 Get a current LockToken immediately before the write and confirm the P1…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --query '{LockToken:LockToken, RateRuleAction:WebACL.Rules[?Name==`AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300-CreatedByCloudFront`].Action}'
```
**Purpose:** Get a current LockToken immediately before the write and confirm the P1 rate rule is still Action=Count. The token changes after every write and must be current or UpdateWebACL fails with WAFOptimisticLockException.
**Advisory:** Use the LockToken returned here (not the one from the investigation) in the apply step; it is single-use per write.

### Step 3: Apply

#### 3.1 Create the WAF IP set holding the two confirmed-malicious IPs for the…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 create-ip-set --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --name example-shop-malicious-ips --description "Confirmed malicious IPs: card tester 198.51.100.30 and path/secret scanner 198.51.100.20 (incident 2026-10-10)" --ip-address-version IPV4 --addresses 198.51.100.30/32 198.51.100.20/32
```
**Purpose:** Create the WAF IP set holding the two confirmed-malicious IPs for the IP-match Block rule (gap C). Record the returned Id/ARN for the update.
**Advisory:** 198.51.100.10 (likely sanctioned Artillery test) and 198.51.100.60 (already blocked by CommonRuleSet) are deliberately excluded; do not add 198.51.100.10 without the load-test owner's confirmation.

#### 3.2 Apply all three changes in one atomic UpdateWebACL
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 update-web-acl --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --default-action Allow={} --lock-token <FRESH_LOCK_TOKEN_FROM_PRE_VALIDATE> --visibility-config SampledRequestsEnabled=true,CloudWatchMetricsEnabled=true,MetricName=CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --rules file://waf-rules-hardened.json
```
**Purpose:** Apply all three changes in one atomic UpdateWebACL. Build waf-rules-hardened.json from the prepare backup and edit only: (A) rule AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300 Action Count→Block (keep Limit=300/300s/IP); (B) add a Priority-6 RateBasedStatement Block rule, Limit=100/300s/IP, with a ScopeDownStatement ByteMatch on UriPath EXACTLY "/checkout/payment"; (C) add a Priority-7 IPSetReferenceStatement Block rule for example-shop-malicious-ips. Preserve all five managed rule groups (P0 AntiDDoS, P2 IpReputation, P3 Common, P4 KnownBadInputs, P5 SQLi) and priorities. Each new rule needs its own VisibilityConfig.
**Risks:** Count→Block will throttle ANY single IP over 300 req/300s, including 198.51.100.10 if it is a sanctioned load test — confirm with the owner first, or expect that test traffic to be blocked., An overly low /checkout/payment limit could block legitimate high-volume checkout clients behind a shared NAT egress IP; start conservative and tune via WAF sampled requests + CloudWatch.
**Advisory:** A stale LockToken causes WAFOptimisticLockException — re-run pre_validate and retry., WAF changes propagate to CloudFront edges within a few minutes; validate after propagation.

### Step 4: Post Validate

#### 4.1 Confirm AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300 now shows Action=Block, the new…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --query 'WebACL.Rules[].{Name:Name,Priority:Priority,Action:Action,Override:OverrideAction}'
```
**Purpose:** Confirm AWS-RateBasedRule-IP-300 now shows Action=Block, the new /checkout/payment rate rule and IP-deny rule are present, and all five managed rule groups remain at their original priorities.
**Advisory:** Allow a few minutes for edge propagation before interpreting live traffic.

#### 4.2 Verify the gaps are closed in practice and watch for false positives…
**Type:** text
Inspect WAF logs in Athena table default.waf_logs (bucket aws-waf-logs-012345678901_1) and per-rule CloudWatch metrics to confirm the rate-based and IP-deny rules register BLOCK for abusive sources while legitimate checkout traffic is not blocked. Tune the /checkout/payment Limit and consider lowering the global rate Limit from observed baselines.
**Purpose:** Verify the gaps are closed in practice and watch for false positives before considering the mitigation complete.
**Advisory:** Consider AWS Bot Control or a CAPTCHA/Challenge on the checkout path as defense-in-depth against browser-spoofed card testing.

### Step 5: Rollback

#### 5.1 Fetch a fresh LockToken before reverting, since the apply step changed…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --query LockToken --output text
```
**Purpose:** Fetch a fresh LockToken before reverting, since the apply step changed it.

#### 5.2 Restore the original rule set from the prepare backup (extract…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 update-web-acl --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --default-action Allow={} --lock-token <FRESH_LOCK_TOKEN> --visibility-config SampledRequestsEnabled=true,CloudWatchMetricsEnabled=true,MetricName=CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --rules file://<RULES_FROM_PREPARE_BACKUP>.json
```
**Purpose:** Restore the original rule set from the prepare backup (extract WebACL.Rules into the --rules file) if the hardened config blocks legitimate traffic. The new IP set can be left or deleted with delete-ip-set once unreferenced.
**Risks:** Rolling back re-opens the rate/abuse control gaps; use only if legitimate-traffic impact outweighs the protection, and plan a corrected re-apply.

## Code Change Specification

### Requirements

#### 1. Persist the hardened WAF rate/abuse controls in the Web ACL's infrastructure-as-code definition so they are not lost to drift or a redeploy.
**Description:** The gaps were closed by manual UpdateWebACL. If CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 is managed by IaC (CDK/CloudFormation/Terraform), codify: (1) the rate-based rule Action=Block; (2) the scoped-down /checkout/payment rate Block rule; (3) the malicious-IP IP set + IP-match Block rule. If the ACL is auto-generated by CloudFront (CreatedByCloudFront- prefix), move it to an explicitly managed definition so these settings persist, since a regenerated ACL may revert to Count mode.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- The IaC declares the rate-based rule with Action=Block and matching Limit/EvaluationWindow.
- The IaC includes the per-endpoint /checkout/payment rate Block rule and the malicious-IP IP set with its IP-match Block rule.
- A fresh deploy produces a Web ACL whose GetWebACL output matches the hardened config (rate rule Block, new rules present, five managed groups intact), with no reversion to Count mode.
